from collections import Counter

def find_lines(grid, axis=0):
    rows = grid if axis == 0 else [list(col) for col in zip(*grid)]
    modes=[]
    for seq in rows:
        counts=Counter(seq)
        modes.append(max(counts, key=counts.get))
    candidates=[]
    for color in set(modes):
        inds=[i for i,x in enumerate(modes) if x==color]
        if len(inds)>=2 and len(set(b-a for a,b in zip(inds,inds[1:])))==1:
            candidates.append((len(inds), color, inds))
    if not candidates:
        raise ValueError(('no periodic boundary', modes))
    # In these diagrams grid lines form the regular, less frequent modal-color sequence.
    candidates.sort(key=lambda x:(x[0], -x[2][1]+x[2][0]))
    return candidates[0][2]

def transform(grid):
    R,C=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    rs=find_lines(grid,0); cs=find_lines(grid,1)
    crossings=[grid[r][c] for r in rs for c in cs]
    boundary=Counter(crossings).most_common(1)[0][0]
    marks=[(i,j,grid[r][c]) for i,r in enumerate(rs) for j,c in enumerate(cs) if grid[r][c]!=boundary]
    if not marks: raise ValueError('no marker crossings')
    r0=min(x[0] for x in marks); r1=max(x[0] for x in marks)
    c0=min(x[1] for x in marks); c1=max(x[1] for x in marks)
    fill=Counter(grid[r][c] for r in range(R) if r not in set(rs) for c in range(C) if c not in set(cs)).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out=[]
    for i in range(r0,r1):
        row=[]
        for j in range(c0,c1):
            vals=(grid[rs[i]][cs[j]],grid[rs[i]][cs[j+1]],grid[rs[i+1]][cs[j]],grid[rs[i+1]][cs[j+1]])
            row.append(vals[0] if vals[0]!=boundary and len(set(vals))==1 else fill)
        out.append(row)
    return out

program='''from collections import Counter


def _grid_lines(grid, axis):
    sequences = grid if axis == 0 else [list(col) for col in zip(*grid)]
    modes = [Counter(seq).most_common(1)[0][0] for seq in sequences]
    candidates = []
    for color in set(modes):
        indices = [i for i, value in enumerate(modes) if value == color]
        if len(indices) >= 2 and len({b - a for a, b in zip(indices, indices[1:])}) == 1:
            candidates.append((len(indices), indices))
    if not candidates:
        raise ValueError("Could not identify regular grid lines")
    return min(candidates, key=lambda item: item[0])[1]


def transform(grid):
    height, width = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    rows = _grid_lines(grid, 0)
    cols = _grid_lines(grid, 1)

    line_colors = [Counter(grid[r]).most_common(1)[0][0] for r in rows]
    line_colors.extend(
        Counter(grid[r][c] for r in range(height)).most_common(1)[0][0]
        for c in cols
    )
    boundary = Counter(line_colors).most_common(1)[0][0]

    marked = [
        (i, j)
        for i, r in enumerate(rows)
        for j, c in enumerate(cols)
        if grid[r][c] != boundary
    ]
    r0 = min(i for i, _ in marked)
    r1 = max(i for i, _ in marked)
    c0 = min(j for _, j in marked)
    c1 = max(j for _, j in marked)

    row_lines = set(rows)
    col_lines = set(cols)
    fill = Counter(
        grid[r][c]
        for r in range(height) if r not in row_lines
        for c in range(width) if c not in col_lines
    ).most_common(1)[0][0]

    output = []
    for i in range(r0, r1):
        out_row = []
        for j in range(c0, c1):
            corners = (
                grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]],
            )
            out_row.append(corners[0] if corners[0] != boundary and len(set(corners)) == 1 else fill)
        output.append(out_row)
    return output
'''
